The next day!

Ran woke up early, got dressed, and went out to prepare breakfast.

"Good morning, sister Ran," said Conan, rubbing his eyes and yawning.

"Good morning, Conan. Didn't you sleep well last night?"

"Yes, I'm not used to it."

Conan smiled bitterly to himself. Mouri Kogoro's snores were louder than thunder; it would be a miracle to sleep well.

At that moment, Heiji opened the door, followed by a sleepy Kazuha. Both were already dressed.

Kazuha had woken up early, gone back to Heiji's room, and snuggled into his arms for a little nap.

"Good morning, sister Kazuha. Good morning, brother Heiji."

Conan felt completely resigned; acting like a child was too hard for him.

"Good morning, Ran. Good morning, Conan," said Kazuha with her eyes still half-closed from sleep.

"Good morning, Kazuha. Good morning, Heiji," replied Ran with a sweet smile.

"Good morning, Ran. What are you doing up so early, brat?"

[Hehe~]

Conan rolled his eyes. He had realized that Heiji loved teasing him.

Ran was an excellent cook, and breakfast was delicious.

"Case of rank C 'Find the missing Kudo Shinichi' not completed on time. 10 evil points added. Evil value remains in an extremely dangerous state. Host is advised to reconsider their actions accordingly."

Suddenly, a virtual character attribute bar appeared before Heiji's eyes.

Heiji felt completely resigned. Basically, the rank C train case had been useless. Although it was normal; that mission was very easy for him, but he simply didn't want to do it. And if he didn't want to, it was fair to receive the corresponding punishment.

But...

[System, have you changed your personality? Now you care about me?]

However, silence reigned in his mind. If it wasn't related to a mission, the system wouldn't appear.

"Morning news: According to police sources, the famous Italian thieves group, the Cabana Group, has illegally entered Japan, along with fifteen thousand Maple Leaf gold coins that the Italian bank was preparing to issue a year ago..."

Everyone who was having breakfast was drawn to the content of the news.

"Fifteen thousand gold coins, how much money would that be? If they gave it all to me, then... hehe..." Mouri Kogoro's classic expression appeared.

"Dad..." Ran looked at Mouri Kogoro with resignation.

"I've heard those fifteen thousand gold coins are worth one hundred million," Conan suddenly said.

"One hundred... one hundred million?" Mouri Kogoro shouted, astonished.

"Wow, that's a lot of money," Kazuha said.

Heiji was watching TV without understanding, not paying attention to what was being said.

Because the system had another mission for him.

Ding~~

"Rank C mission: Steal the fifteen thousand Maple Leaf gold coins from under the police's noses. Time limit: just tonight. Success reward: Criminal skill Sliding Flight. Failure penalty: 10 evil points. Serious warning: the host is already in an extremely dangerous state. If the mission fails, the evil value will overflow, and the host will be eliminated."

Heiji hadn't expected that watching TV could activate a mission.

[Sliding Flight? System, explain the function of this skill.]

The system didn't respond with words, but two lines of text appeared before Heiji's eyes.

[Skill name: Sliding Flight.]

[Principle: Like a hang glider, it requires a fall from a high place to form an air current around the body and control it to glide through the air. Unlike a hang glider, the host can use jumps to accelerate the airflow, thus speeding up the glide.]

This explanation made Heiji's pulse quicken. If he got this skill, wouldn't that mean he'd be a human hang glider? Jumping from one building to another... the feeling would be absolutely amazing.

"Heiji, what's wrong with you? Why are you breathing so fast?" Kazuha suddenly asked, concerned.

Heiji came to his senses and smiled gently at Kazuha, "It's nothing, I also think it's a lot of money."

[Looks like I'll have to think carefully about this mission. The reward is too good.]

For Mouri Kogoro and the others, the news was just an interlude that they soon forgot.

"Kazuha, where do you and Heiji want to go to have fun? I can be your guide."

After washing the dishes, Ran approached Kazuha and asked expectantly.

"Well, I haven't thought about it. Heiji, what about you?" Kazuha looked at Heiji.

Heiji set aside his thoughts and wrapped his arm around her waist, "Where do you want to go?"

"I want to go shopping, but I've also heard that Tokyo's snacks are delicious. Heiji, what should I do?" Kazuha was very indecisive.

"Silly, we'll go shopping today and eat snacks tomorrow."

"Really? You're so nice, Heiji!"

Ran looked at Kazuha with envy, "Heiji treats Kazuha so well. He's such a sweet guy."

[This guy, Hattori, showing off his love in front of a kid.]

Conan looked at Heiji with disdain, with a sullen face.

Tokyo is one of Japan's largest cities and an international metropolis. The dazzling variety of products was overwhelming.

"Ran, look! Do you like this dress?"

"Yes, it's very pretty. I'm sure Kazuha would look even prettier in it."

"I think it would look good on Ran too. After all, you have a great body."

"You think? Kazuha's too."

Heiji walked carefreely behind them, accompanying the two girls as they wandered through several clothing stores.

"Ran, look, how beautiful those two scarves are!"

Passing by a store in the mall, through the transparent window, they saw two beautiful scarves hanging alone. Their design was elegant and sophisticated, perfect for high school students like Kazuha and Ran.

"You're right, they're so pretty."

The beautiful eyes of the two girls sparkled as they stared at the scarves.

"If you like them, why don't you go in and check them out? What are you doing standing there?"

"But Heiji, it's a brand store, those scarves must be very expensive," Kazuha whispered.

Heiji looked up and saw the logo on the door: Chanel.

"It's just Chanel. A scarf will cost at most tens of thousands of yen. I'll buy it for you."

"No, it's fine. Ran, let's go."

However, Kazuha pulled Heiji and led him away.

Ran covered her mouth behind her to laugh secretly, "Kazuha is upset that Heiji spends money."

As they passed by a store, Heiji's eyes lit up. A plan, a criminal plan, started to form in his mind.

"Since Shinichi isn't here, we won't bother you any longer. Professor Agasa, and Conan, we're leaving now," said Ran, somewhat disappointed.

"Wait a moment, Ran. Conan's parents had an accident and are in the hospital, and it's not appropriate for me, being a single man, to take care of him. I was wondering if he could stay at your house for a while and be taken care of," said Professor Agasa with a smile.

Ran looked at Conan uncertainly. "Well, I guess so, but first I need to ask my father."

"Thank you so much for the trouble, Ran. Conan, hurry up and go with Sister Ran," said Professor Agasa, winking at Conan.

Conan rolled his eyes at Professor Agasa, but remembering what had happened earlier, he thought that maybe through Mouri Kogoro, he could investigate those two men in black and find out what poison they had given him.

Since it had rained a little earlier, there were some puddles along the way.

Ran walked absentmindedly, alone and at the back of the group, while Conan, to show his childish nature, stepped into the puddles every now and then, with an appearance of total innocence.

[How long does this guy, Hattori, plan to follow us?]

Conan also felt helpless. If it weren't for Hattori's presence, he wouldn't have to pretend.

Heiji walked in the middle, wrapping his arm around Kazuha. Seeing Conan ahead, a smile appeared on his lips: "Conan, there's another puddle up ahead. Go step in it."

[Damn, this bastard Hattori!]

Conan cursed inwardly but had to act interested outwardly: "Yes, stepping in puddles is so much fun!"

"Heiji, I'm going to talk to Ran for a while."

"Sure, go ahead."

Seeing that Kazuha joined Ran, Heiji quickly strode over to Conan and picked him up in one swift motion.

"Ah, Brother Heiji, put me down!"

"Come on, kid. With those short legs, you're way too slow."

Conan glared ahead, but decided not to resist any further and let Heiji carry him like a dog.

Mouri Detective Agency!

"What? Not only are these two kids staying at our house, but this other kid too?" Upon hearing Ran's words, Mouri Kogoro immediately sobered up from his drunken stupor.

"So what's the problem? Heiji and Kazuha are only staying one night. As for Conan, it's necessary. When his mother comes, we'll ask for child support, and that's it," said Ran dismissively.

"Hmm, I've got nothing against those two high school students, but this kid... I have a feeling the way he looks at you, Ran, is a bit strange."

Mouri Kogoro's gaze made Conan's hair stand on end, and he couldn't help but hide behind Heiji.

"Dad..." Ran said, completely resigned.

"No, no! I don't trust this kid," Mouri Kogoro said, crossing his arms.

"Uncle, my mom says she'll give you a million yen for support later," said Conan innocently.

"I said no... What? A million?! Really?" Mouri Kogoro's eyes lit up.

"Yes, if you don't believe me, you can ask Professor Agasa."

"Ah, if that's the case, then stay. But you'll sleep with me. And remember, tell your mother to bring the million yen soon," Mouri Kogoro said with a greedy smile.

Everyone had a grim expression, completely defeated by his attitude.

Night, deep and silent!

Heiji was lying on the bed, hands behind his head, staring at the ceiling with resignation. Kazuha wasn't beside him; she had been dragged by Ran to sleep with her.

Watching an empty room!

However, this gave Heiji the opportunity to think quietly about a few things.

[Conan's true identity must not be revealed under any circumstances. Once it's revealed, the secret will no longer be one, and no one can guarantee that Ran won't slip up.]

[But relying solely on cases to eliminate the points of evil is a bit slow. I wonder what the other methods might be.]

Heiji's room was right next to Ran's, while Mouri Kogoro's room was on the other side, separated by a large living room.

Ran's room was very simply decorated, but with a touch of romance typical of a young girl.

The two girls were lying on the bed, and the light duvet from the air conditioner perfectly outlined their figures. The duvet was very warm, and even in winter, it didn't feel cold.

"What? Kazuha, you and Heiji never held hands before you became a couple?" Ran whispered.

Kazuha nodded shyly.

"My goodness! With the way Heiji treats you, and you never let him hold your hand?"

In Ran's mind, if Heiji treated Kazuha so well, even if they weren't a couple, they should have been very close. She was surprised that they had never held hands.

"At that time, I wasn't sure about Heiji's feelings. If he was too casual, I was afraid he might see me as an easy girl," Kazuha whispered.

In reality, there was another reason: the original Hattori Heiji was also a novice with no idea about anything. A virgin's world is always very pure.

"Ran, you feel the same way, don't you?" Kazuha whispered.

"Huh?" Ran didn't quite understand.

"I noticed that you're wearing safety shorts under your skirt. Is it so that other boys won't see you?" Kazuha joked. "Heiji told me that boys are very selfish with the girls they like; they don't want anyone else taking advantage of them, not even with a glance."

"Ah, no! It's out of habit. Since I practice karate, I often do karate moves without realizing it, and it would be very embarrassing if my skirt flew up and my underwear showed, so I wear safety shorts," Ran hurriedly explained, though a thought crossed her mind.

"Kazuha..."

A soft call came from beneath the blankets.

"What is it, Ran?" Kazuha asked, puzzled.

"Do boys really not like it when girls get too close to other boys?" Ran asked, her face blushing.

"And not just to other boys, not even to kids like Conan! I'm not sure about Kudo, but Heiji doesn't like it when I get close to other men, and of course, I don't either."

When talking about Heiji, even in the darkness, Ran could almost see the happy smile on Kazuha's face. Silently, a thought was reaffirmed in her heart.

[Shinichi wouldn't like it if I got too close to other people, would he?]

"What an adorable child."

It was undeniable that after shrinking, Conan was really very cute.

"What's your name?"

Ran approached, asking curiously. Since Heiji was in front of her blocking the way, she didn't attempt to hug Conan.

"My name is... my name is Edogawa Conan," Conan said, improvising a name that came out of his mouth in an instant of inspiration.

"Oh, really? That name, the more I look at it, seems like it was made up on the spot. Do you really call yourself that?" Heiji asked skeptically.

Conan's face changed and he became very nervous. "Damn Hattori! What's this guy doing with Ran?"

"It's because my mom is a fan of Conan Doyle, so she gave me this name," Conan responded innocently.

"Ran, don't you think this kid looks a lot like Kudo?"

Kazuha said as she approached, a hint of doubt in her eyes. Since it was the first time she saw Kudo Shinichi, she didn't have the familiarity that distorts perception. Conan was basically a miniature version of Kudo Shinichi, so naturally, there wasn't much of a difference.

A cold sweat ran down Conan's back, and he felt his heart skip a beat.

"But Shinichi never told me he had a relative who looked so much like him," Ran said, surprised.

"I don't know if this kid is related to Kudo, but what I do know is that he has been at his house."

Feeling all eyes on him, Heiji collected his thoughts and began explaining.

"Kazuha, Ran, do you remember how the iron gate was when we arrived at Kudo's house?"

"It was open," Kazuha said quietly.

"Exactly. The door is electric. With that type of switch, if you're not tall enough, it's easy to open it, but hard to close it. And I noticed that the height at which the button is installed is impossible for this kid to reach."

Everyone was confused; even Conan didn't understand where Heiji was going with this.

"Heiji, what are you trying to say?" Kazuha asked, pulling on Heiji's hand.

"Relax, let me finish."

Heiji looked at Conan and smiled strangely, making Conan break out in cold sweat.

"When entering the yard, I noticed there was a very clear trail of footprints on the grass. They weren't the footprints of an adult, but of a child. However, those footprints were a bit strange, because above them, there was a shallow dragging mark, like what would happen if the pants were too long."

Conan's pupils contracted sharply as he looked at Heiji in horror.

[This guy, Hattori! How did he figure that out? I was so careful!]

When his body shrank, his clothes, naturally, were too big for him. It was inevitable that the cuffs of his pants dragged on the grass as he walked. But Conan would swear that those marks weren't easy to detect.

"At first, I wasn't too sure, but after seeing a faint water stain on the floor of the house, I confirmed it completely. This kid..."

Heiji suddenly lifted Conan. His strange expression terrified Conan to the core, and he almost peed himself.

[Hattori, no...]

"If he's not a relative of Kudo, then he's definitely a thief who broke in to steal clothes from his house."

"Ah..."

Conan was frozen. He thought Heiji already knew his identity, and the scare almost killed him.

[This bastard Hattori!]

"This kid took the clothes Kudo wore when he was little and left, but since he wasn't tall enough, he couldn't close the door. Am I wrong, little clothes thief?" Heiji said, holding Conan in the air.

"Ah, you're so bad, big brother! Brother Shinichi gave me permission, I'm not a thief."

Conan let out a big sigh of relief; he almost died from the scare.

"Conan is a distant relative of Shinichi, and it's true he came with Shinichi's permission," the Professor Agasa quickly explained from the side.

"Ah, so he's a relative of the Kudo family. No wonder he looks so much like him," Ran nodded.

"You're a very rude child. You should call him 'Brother Heiji,' you can't just call him by his name," Kazuha was concerned about this.

"Okay, I'm sorry, Brother Heiji. Put me down now," Conan continued with his childish act.

Heiji stared at Conan for a while, until the kid started feeling uncomfortable. Only then did he carelessly put him down, with a doubtful expression. "And why would this kid wear clothes that are so big for his size?"

"Ah, you must be Sister Ran, right? Brother Shinichi told me to tell you that he's working on a very complicated case, so he won't be back for a while, so that Sister Ran doesn't worry."

Conan quickly changed the subject. If Heiji kept going down this path, he'd end up peeing himself. If this guy, with his sharp observation skills, figured out his identity, both he and Ran would be in danger.

"How did Shinichi tell you that? Has he come back?"

Heiji nodded to the side. Ran's intelligence kicked in.

Conan's expression tightened, but his mind raced. "Professor Agasa told me, and asked me to pass it on to Sister Ran."

"Really?" Ran asked skeptically.

Conan nodded vigorously, with an expression of total innocence.

"I just can't believe it! Why didn't Shinichi call me to tell me?"

Seeing Ran's gloomy expression, Conan felt the urge to tell her everything, not caring about the consequences.

"Ran..."

"Professor Agasa, I just saw two men in black coats pass by your door. Are they your friends?"

When Heiji heard Conan's words, he stopped dead in his tracks, a look of horror in his eyes.

[Black coats?]

His breath caught in his throat.

"Brother Heiji, what did they look like?"

"Well, since it's night, I couldn't see them clearly, but one was tall and thin, and the other was stocky. They didn't seem like good people."

[It's them, it has to be them. They've come to investigate my house. Have they figured out that I'm not dead? No, if they left without making a sound, it means they found nothing. I can't say anything now, or Ran will be in serious danger.]

"Conan, from now on, you have to call me 'Sister Ran,' you can't just call your elders by their first names," Ran scolded him seriously.

Conan responded innocently. He didn't see the fleeting smile that appeared on Heiji's lips.

[Little Shinigami of Elementary School, you're my guarantee for getting rid of that enormous amount of evil points. How could I let you reveal the truth so easily?]

It was clear that the story about the two men in black was a fabrication of Heiji's. As for whether that made him evil, he didn't care. If you don't look after yourself, heaven and earth will destroy you. He had never pretended to be a saint.

If helping others puts you in danger, that's not greatness, that's being an idiot.

"Heiji, Shinichi still hasn't answered the phone, what should I do?

At that moment, Ran didn't resemble the karate champion at all; she was simply a helpless high school student.

Seeing the helpless look on Ran's face, Heiji sighed, grabbed a coat from the side, and threw it to her. "Come on, take me to Kudo's house to check it out."

Ran's eyes lit up with joy. She jumped up and gratefully nodded at Heiji. "Thank you, Heiji."

Heiji called Kazuha, explained the situation, and asked her to quickly bundle up.

Since it was already winter, both girls wore long coats. Ran wore a short skirt with black tights that tightly wrapped around her slender, pale legs, while Kazuha wore tight nine-point pants that perfectly outlined her straight legs. Both wore knee-high boots, the favorite footwear for girls in winter.

The two young women radiated an air of youth, purity, and beauty.

Ran informed a completely drunk Mouri Kogoro and then left with Heiji and Kazuha.

"Ran, what time did you part ways with Kudo?"

Heiji wrapped his arm around Kazuha, protecting her from the cold night wind.

"I think it was around six in the afternoon. He left suddenly, in a rush." At that moment, Ran wasn't thinking about anything else; her mind was entirely consumed with worry for Kudo Shinichi.

"It's only 8:30 now, so it's only been two and a half hours. Maybe he just stepped out; you don't need to worry so much."

Of course, Heiji was just trying to console Ran. By this time, Kudo Shinichi had already disappeared; only Edogawa Conan existed.

Ran forced a smile and looked at Heiji with sadness. "But I have a bad feeling, like something really happened to Shinichi."

"Ran, maybe you're imagining things. With Heiji here, he'll surely help you find Kudo," said Kazuha, completely confident in her boyfriend.

Heiji smiled slightly. This time, he really couldn't do anything. He would never reveal the fact that Kudo Shinichi had become Edogawa Conan.

Even if it meant not completing the system's mission, he didn't care. It was just 10 evil points. As long as the "Little Shinigami of Elementary School" was nearby, the cases would be endless.

Maybe this C-rank case, "Finding the Missing Kudo Shinichi," was just a trap set by the system, specifically designed to make him accumulate evil points.

The three walked for half an hour and finally arrived at Kudo Shinichi's house.

During the walk, thanks to Heiji's guidance, Ran regained her usual composure and stopped worrying so much.

Ding-dong!!!! Ding-dong!!!!

They rang the doorbell several times, but no one answered. The house was completely dark. Ran's heart tightened again.

Heiji frowned, gently pushed the iron gate, and, to his surprise, it opened immediately.

"The door's not locked, should we go in?"

Ran was stunned. Seeing the questioning look from Heiji, she nodded slightly.

Since it had just rained a little, the ground was somewhat damp. As they climbed the steps, Heiji's gaze sharpened for a moment, and then he walked toward the main door of the house without changing his expression.

He let go of Kazuha and grabbed the door handle. There were water stains on it.

The door was open. Heiji entered, and Ran followed with Kazuha.

"Ran, turn on the light. Be careful where you step, try to walk in a straight line and make sure your steps are even."

Although Ran didn't understand why, she nodded. After a moment, the light turned on, illuminating the entire house.

Heiji walked on the wooden floor, his gaze fixed, observing everything around him.

Meanwhile, at Professor Agasa's house, Kudo Shinichi, now turned into Conan, was startled and looked horrified at his own house.

"Professor Agasa, the lights in my house are on!"

He was scared, unsure if it was those two men in black. A chill ran down his spine.

"Could it be that Ran has come to look for you?" Professor Agasa didn't overthink it like Conan.

Conan froze for a moment. Thinking it over, he understood. If it were the men in black, they wouldn't act so conspicuously. It had to be that girl, Ran.

"Phew, I almost died from the scare because of Ran."

"Shinichi, if Ran has come to look for you, you should go see her. Isn't her father a detective? Maybe you could use his identity to find those two men in black and return to normal."

Professor Agasa's words made Conan pause for a moment, then he sank into deep thought.

"Professor Agasa, I understand."

At Kudo Shinichi's house.

"Shinichi still hasn't returned."

Ran had searched the whole house, but there was no sign that Kudo Shinichi had come back.

Heiji shook his head. "Ran, does Kudo have any other friends nearby?"

Although he already had a suspicion, he wanted to confirm it. Had Kudo Shinichi really turned into Edogawa Conan?

When Ran heard Heiji's words, it seemed like she woke from a trance. Her face lit up with joy, and she ran off with her long legs. "Shinichi gets along really well with Professor Agasa next door, he often goes to his house!"

Her voice was still echoing, but she was already gone.

Professor Agasa's house was a modern-style villa, full of technology everywhere.

"Ran, what are you doing here?"

Professor Agasa, with his big belly, came out and greeted Ran with joy.

"Professor Agasa, is Shinichi at your house?" Ran looked around but didn't see any trace of Kudo Shinichi.

"Shinichi, no, he's not here."

"Not here?" Ran immediately felt disappointed.

At that moment, Heiji entered, pulling Kazuha along. He glanced at the boy with glasses, Conan, and a smile spread across his lips.

"This kid must be related to Kudo, right?"

Heiji approached Conan and stared at him.

"Ho... hello, big brother," Conan responded in a small voice. He felt an indescribable sense of embarrassment.

"Don't give me any greetings. Have you been to the house next door today?"

The house next door, of course, referred to Kudo Shinichi's house. Although Heiji didn't plan to reveal this kid's identity, a little mental game wouldn't hurt.

"How could Kudo do something like this? How could he let you go home alone?" Kazuha said, astonished.

"Shinichi is a deduction fanatic, there's nothing to be done, I'm used to it," Ran said with resignation.

Heiji silently listened from the side. The reason why Kudo Shinichi had left so suddenly was something he knew very well. It seemed like the "Little Primary School Shinigami" was about to make his debut.

The three of them left the amusement park together. At Ran's invitation, Kazuha dragged Heiji to her house, and even upon learning that there was a free room, she insisted on spending the night there.

But...

Heiji didn't think the same. He had planned to do "adult things" with Kazuha that night.

Along the way, the two girls chatted nonstop, as if they were good friends who hadn't seen each other in a long time.

Heiji followed them on the side, bored and lost in thought.

[Kudo Shinichi's departure means that the plot is about to begin. With the appearance of the "Little Primary School Shinigami," there will be endless cases.]

[It seems that, even if I don't become friends with Conan, it wouldn't be wise to be his enemy. After all, I can rely on him to get an endless flow of cases.]

[And only with cases can I eliminate that damn evil value.]

[However, relying solely on cases to eliminate the evil value will take an eternity. Even if they were S-rank cases, I would need 99 to completely eliminate it. I don't think that cheating system would be so kind as to give me that many S-rank cases. I remember the system said there were other ways to eliminate the evil value; it seems I'll have to investigate those other methods more thoroughly...]

"What? You and Kudo haven't even held hands?" Kazuha's surprised shout pulled Heiji out of his thoughts. Ran nodded timidly, both resigned and embarrassed.

"If you haven't even held hands, what kind of childhood friends are you?" Kazuha murmured to herself.

"Ahem, ahem."

Heiji cleared his throat dryly from the side, and Kazuha's face immediately turned red. She had forgotten that, if it hadn't been for Heiji's initiative recently, her situation would have been very similar.

Before Heiji "crossed the line," Kazuha and the Heiji back then were in the same situation: they hadn't even held hands. At that moment, the current Heiji was stunned... no, pleasantly surprised.

A girl should be pure.

"Wow, looks like Kazuha has her own secrets too. Tell me everything," Ran quickly changed the subject to divert attention.

Amid the banter between the two girls, the three of them soon arrived at Ran's house, which was also the Mouri Detective Agency.

Clang!

"Dad, I'm back."

The three entered the agency and were left speechless.

A middle-aged man with several days' worth of stubble was slumped in an office chair. The desk in front of him, the floor, and the surroundings were filled with beer cans and takeout food boxes. The whole room was a mess.

Heiji was speechless. It was a miracle that Mouri Kogoro was still alive. The number of beer cans could fill an entire bathtub.

[There definitely should be no logic in the world of Conan.]

Ran had a grim look on her face, clenching her fists tightly. She walked over with her long, white legs to the desk: "Dad, what a bad impression for the guests to see you like this."

"Don't start with that. I'm the great detective Mouri Kogoro. I choose the cases, not the other way around," Mouri Kogoro said, completely drunk.

"Of course! No wonder Mom left you. You're always drunk," Ran complained.

Kazuha gently tugged at Ran: "Hey, did Ran's mom divorce your dad?"

Ran smiled faintly and shook her head: "No, they're just separated."

Heiji made a face on the side. They were definitely separated, but it had been like that for ten years. Thinking of Eri Kisaki, he felt a certain fantasy: a mature and seductive wife, the undefeated queen of the legal world, her charm was no small thing.

Screech~~

"You can stay in this room tonight," Ran said, leading them to a room.

"What?!" Kazuha exclaimed, somewhat embarrassed.

"Kazuha, why is your face so red? You and Heiji...?"

Ran couldn't finish her sentence. She was also a young maiden, and couldn't say such things out loud.

"Don't worry, this room is fine."

A room was a room. Anyway, Heiji wasn't going to take Kazuha in the house of Ran. They were just going to sleep in the same bed, it wasn't like they hadn't done it before.

However, it was obvious that Kazuha's mind was thinking of something else. She stood to the side, head down and face red, not saying a word.

After 8 p.m., Heiji came out of the bathroom after his shower and saw Ran sitting next to the phone with a worried expression, so he approached.

"Ran, it's your turn to shower."

"Heiji, what should I do? I called Shinichi's house and he's not answering. What if something happened to him?"

Heiji froze for a moment. By then, Kudo Shinichi had probably already become Edogawa Conan.

Ding~~!!!

Suddenly, the system's voice resonated in his mind.

"Case of rank C detected: Find the missing Kudo Shinichi. Time limit: one day. If not completed on time, corresponding evil value will be added."

Heiji was stunned, his face darkening.

[Damn, system, you can't be more cheating! What the hell does Kudo Shinichi have to do with you?]

"Please complete the mission on time. Otherwise, 10 points of evil value will be added," the system's voice was mechanical and relentless.

[But right now, Kudo Shinichi has already disappeared, only Edogawa Conan exists. Isn't this mission a blatant trap?] Heiji thought, gritting his teeth.

The system fell silent for a moment.

"Mission of rank C detected: Find the missing Kudo Shinichi. Please find Kudo Shinichi or reveal his new identity within one day. If not completed on time, corresponding evil value will be added."

After that, the system fell silent once more.

Heiji was speechless. Revealing Edogawa Conan's true identity... what the hell was that supposed to mean?

If he revealed it, would he still be the "Little Primary School Shinigami"?

"How did you know, Hattori?"

"How did you know, young Hattori?"

Kudo Shinichi and Inspector Megure both asked at the same time, surprised.

Heiji didn't want to pay attention at first, but then he thought better of it: the more fame he had, the more important cases he would have access to, and a more important case could be an S-rank case.

S-rank cases were tied to 1000 points of evil. If he solved several cases like that, that enormous number of evil points wouldn't seem so terrifying anymore.

Heiji let go of Kazuha, but continued holding her hand. It was her first time being so close to a corpse, so it was normal for her to be scared. However, that wouldn't stop him from solving the case.

"Sir, we found a sharp knife with blood in this young lady's bag!"

At that moment, a police officer shouted from not too far away, pulling a knife from Miss Aiko's bag, which had blood stains.

"What?" Inspector Megure rushed over, nodding repeatedly. "Young Hattori, it seems you were wrong."

"No, I wasn't the murderer, it wasn't me!" Miss Aiko screamed, terrified.

"The evidence is here, you can't deny it. Take her to the station as the main suspect," ordered Inspector Megure.

"Yes, sir."

"It wasn't me, really! I didn't kill Kishiyama!" Miss Aiko collapsed to the ground, terrified.

"Inspector Megure, Miss Aiko isn't the murderer. It's impossible to decapitate a human with that knife, especially for a woman."

Kudo Shinichi was about to speak, but was interrupted once again by Heiji.

"Then, young Hattori, if you think Miss Hitomi is the murderer, you'll have to find evidence. Otherwise, you're making things very difficult for us," said Inspector Megure resignedly.

"Exactly, I'm not the murderer! Besides, I was sitting in the front row, how could I have killed Kishiyama in the third row?" Hitomi defended herself, nervously.

Heiji looked at Hitomi. In his past life, he was an assassin, he didn't have a soft or compassionate heart, and he wasn't going to forgive her just because she was a woman.

"Inspector Megure, please bring me some hemp rope and a hook. Also, I ask that you interpret the late Mr. Kishiyama and sit in the place he occupied."

"Understood."

Soon, Inspector Megure prepared everything as Heiji instructed.

Seeing this, Kudo Shinichi knew his rival had already solved the case. He crossed his arms, with nothing to do, and prepared to watch the show.

"Kudo, come here and impersonate Miss Hitomi."

"Me?" Kudo Shinichi asked, pointing to himself.

"Of course, didn't you want to be Holmes's assistant? Go ahead."

Kazuha's mood was still unstable, and Heiji wasn't going to let his girl suffer injustice over such a small case.

"The assistant of Holmes? Then I'd be Watson. What a guy," Kudo Shinichi grimaced in disgust but approached without further delay.

"I guess now Kudo is going to give the explanation, right?"

"Ah, if young Hattori hadn't mentioned it, I would have forgotten. Young Kudo, surely you knew the truth from the beginning, right?" That's when Inspector Megure remembered Kudo Shinichi.

"Yes..." Kudo Shinichi replied resignedly.

He then proceeded to show step by step how Hitomi had killed Kishiyama.

"It's true that this method could kill Mr. Kishiyama, but what about the evidence? Where is the evidence?" Hitomi screamed.

"Miss Hitomi, what about your necklace?" Heiji said calmly.

As if struck by lightning, Hitomi froze in place, and tears began to flow uncontrollably.

"Why did he have to abandon me? Why did he have to abandon me?!"

"Young Hattori, young Kudo, thank you so much for your help this time. I'll find a chance to properly thank you. Now, I'll take the culprit."

"I don't need your thanks," said Kudo Shinichi with a bitter smile.

"Fool, are you still scared?" Heiji pinched Kazuha's nose gently.

"But well! It was so close, it'd be weird if I wasn't scared," Kazuha complained in a spoiled way.

"You should train your courage a bit. Look, Ran isn't scared."

Upon hearing Heiji's compliment, Ran smiled bitterly. It wasn't that she wasn't scared, it's just that being scared didn't help.

"Ran is the national karate champion, how could she be scared?" Kudo Shinichi laughed from the side.

"!!! Shinichi!!!" Ran glared at Kudo Shinichi, feeling somewhat offended.

After that, Heiji took Kazuha away to continue having fun.

Although Kudo Shinichi was very interested in Heiji, he didn't stick to him. After all, the distance between Osaka and Tokyo wasn't much, and they would have plenty of time to see each other in the future.

Before he knew it, night fell.

"Heiji, I'm so tired."

After several hours of fun, Kazuha was exhausted.

"Of course, with a certain someone who kept shouting 'let's go to this one!' and 'now to that one!', it'd be weird if you weren't tired," Heiji said, wrapping his arm around her small waist while smiling.

"I really wanted to go on everything. It's my first time out with Heiji, so of course, I wanted to have fun. Because... you're the person I like the most, Heiji," Kazuha said with blushing cheeks.

Looking at her adorable face, Heiji wrapped his arms around her, tilted his head, and kissed her delicate pink lips directly.

"There are a lot of people around... mmm..."

Kazuha soon lost herself in Heiji's tenderness.

Although there were many people around, it wasn't unusual to see a young couple kissing in the street, especially in an amusement park, where it was even more common.

"Um... sorry to interrupt."

Kazuha snapped back to reality suddenly and quickly pulled away from Heiji's embrace, standing aside with her face completely red. She didn't mind when they were alone, but in public, she still maintained the modesty of a young lady.

"R... Ran?"

Seeing that it was Ran, Kazuha sighed in relief. At least it was someone she knew.

"Kazuha, you look so happy," Ran's expression was somewhat forced.

"What's wrong, Ran? And where's that Kudo?" Kazuha quickly took Ran's hand.

"He suddenly said he had something to take care of, rushed off, and told me to go home first."

Ran was somewhat disappointed. She had been waiting for this date for a long time, but Shinichi's behavior had been a great disappointment.

The roller coaster had five rows of seats. In the last row were Gin and Vodka, then Heiji and Kudo Shinichi; in the third row were Hitomi's ex-boyfriend, Kishiyama, and his current girlfriend, Aiko; in the row in front sat Kazuha and Ran, and in the front row were the girl whose hand Kudo Shinichi had taken, Hitomi, and her friend.

Kudo Shinichi, of course, hadn't spoiled Heiji's private moment without a good reason. Although his emotional intelligence regarding his own affairs with Ran was nonexistent, his IQ spiked when it came to other people's matters.

The reason he insisted on sitting with Heiji was because of Gin and Vodka, who were behind them.

"Hattori, don't you really think those two behind us look suspicious?"

Heiji looked at Kudo Shinichi with resignation. He really wanted to tell this curiosity-filled kid: "Of course they're suspicious, and it's something big. In the not-too-distant future you'll become their biggest problem."

But, unfortunately, he couldn't say those words.

"What could be suspicious about them? They just like to wear black and sunglasses. These days there are lots of people who try to look interesting — why do you care?"

Kudo Shinichi frowned. It seemed that this Hattori really hadn't noticed. "Well, never mind, it's not like I want to interfere," he thought.

Heiji avoided looking at Kudo Shinichi. That guy's powers of observation were extremely sharp, and at the slightest lapse he could discover something.

Clack, clack~~

The roller coaster began to move, the sound of iron wheels rumbling as it sped outside.

"AAAahhh!!!"

The roller coaster went up and down, sometimes climbing slowly, sometimes spiraling. The thrilling sensation of being suspended in the air prompted screams throughout the ride.

Heiji didn't scream, but he wore a timely look of excitement.

Kudo Shinichi looked at Heiji, speechless. What was so fun about this roller coaster to make him so excited?

Vodka, seated behind Kudo Shinichi, saw Heiji's expression and felt a certain disdain. He couldn't understand how someone like that had caught his brother Gin's attention; it was obvious he was just a high-school brat.

By contrast, that Kudo Shinichi was far more intimidating.

The roller coaster continued its rapid course. After passing through a vertical loop, it plunged headfirst into a dark tunnel.

Everything was black, so dark you couldn't see your hand in front of your face.

Clack-clack-clack~~

The sound of the roller coaster's movement was very loud, and combined with the whistling wind from the high speed and the screams, it filled the whole tunnel.

"Ah!

A brief cry of pain was quickly drowned by the tide of noise. However, there was someone who noticed that extremely short, odd cry.

A flash of sharpness lit Heiji's eyes: "It smells like blood."

Soon, the roller coaster shot out of the dark tunnel.

Suddenly, a ripping scream was heard, full of terror.

Sitting next to Aiko, Kishiyama... his head had disappeared. The cut was clean at the neck and blood gushed out, splattering part of Kudo Shinichi's clothing.

"AAAahhh!!!

At Aiko's scream, Kazuha and Ran, who were sitting in front of them, turned around and instantly joined the screaming, their faces pale.

The roller coaster returned to the starting station.

"Heiji~~!!

Kazuha clung tightly to Heiji, trembling from head to toe. She had seen dead people before, but seeing one so close — and decapitated at that — had truly terrified her.

Heiji hugged Kazuha, frowning as he looked at the headless corpse. Because of Kudo Shinichi's interference, he had completely forgotten about this incident. Otherwise, he would never have let Kazuha sit in that seat.

Ran looked at Kazuha with envy, searching for Shinichi with her eyes, but she couldn't find him anywhere.

Da, da, da~

Footsteps were heard approaching. Inspector Megure arrived at the scene accompanied by Officer Takagi.

"What happened?"

"While we were on the roller coaster, someone's head was cut off," said Heiji calmly while putting his arm around Kazuha.

"Ah, so it's young Hattori! What are you doing here?"

On seeing Heiji, Inspector Megure appeared incredibly enthusiastic.

"I told you, I came to spend the day with Kazuha," replied Heiji with resignation.

"Oh, right, I had forgotten. So, young Hattori, what do you make of this case?" Inspector Megure asked with interest.

"This is clearly an accident, don't waste our time," Gin said coldly from one side.

Heiji shot Gin a look and then shook his head, addressing Inspector Megure: "This was not an accident. It's a murder case."

"It's a murder case."

At the same time, Kudo Shinichi appeared out of nowhere and said the same thing.

"Well, so young Kudo is here too."

Seeing Kudo Shinichi, Inspector Megure exclaimed in surprise, feeling at the same time a wave of relief. With these two high-school detectives present, he'd only have to handle arresting the culprit.

Kudo Shinichi looked at Heiji, feeling a twinge of rivalry: "He hasn't moved from his spot, how can he be so sure it's a murder?"

"Shinichi, where did you disappear to?" Ran scolded him, annoyed.

"Sorry, sorry, I went to collect evidence," Kudo Shinichi apologized, embarrassed.

"But what are you saying? I was terrified too, and you just..."

Suddenly, Ran fell silent, because Kudo Shinichi had already run over to where Heiji was.

"Hattori, do you want to see who solves this case faster?"

Heiji gave Kudo Shinichi a look: "Don't you already know? This isn't fair to me."

In truth, Heiji had no interest in the case at all, because the system hadn't given him any notification. No notification meant no reward, and no reward meant no motivation. Well, the truth was he was simply too lazy to handle it.

"Relax, relax. How about I give you some time to gather evidence?" said Kudo Shinichi, confident of his victory.

"Hey, hey, young Kudo, if you know it, say it already. Don't keep it to yourself," intervened Inspector Megure, who wasn't in the mood for games.

"Kid, if you know it, say it at once. Don't make us waste time," said Gin, with a cold gleam in his eyes.

Kudo Shinichi's heart leaped. He realized that this man in black was indeed very strange.

"Alright, it seems Hattori won't get his chance. The truth is always one, and the killer is...

"The murderer is Miss Hitomi.

Just as Kudo Shinichi was preparing to announce the culprit, Heiji beat him to it, leaving him with a frozen expression on his face.

After getting on the Great Pendulum, it was already two or three in the afternoon. The two of them arrived at the entrance to the roller coaster.

"Kazuha, Heiji, are you two going to ride the roller coaster as well?"

Ran's cheerful voice came from behind, followed by the sound of footsteps approaching.

"Yes, it looks like you two are too," said Kazuha, just as excited.

"I didn't want to come, I was forced to do so," said Kudo Shinichi reluctantly, not noticing the fleeting shadow of sadness in Ran's gaze.

Heiji shook his head. Kudo Shinichi's deductive ability was strong, but his emotional intelligence was truly at a negative number.

The four met at the entrance, and from there, there was still a ways to go to the area where they could board the roller coaster. Heiji and Kudo Shinichi walked ahead, while Kazuha and Ran followed silently, listening to their conversation.

In reality, it was Kudo Shinichi who was talking to himself, constantly rambling on about Sherlock Holmes.

Heiji had only become a detective out of obligation; he had no real interest in Sherlock Holmes. However, as a mechanic, it was crucial never to reveal one's internal thoughts in any situation. Because of this, even a detective with Kudo Shinichi's sharp perception couldn't notice Heiji's impatience.

"Ran, is Kudo always like this?"

Looking at Kudo Shinichi, who kept talking non-stop, Kazuha was a bit puzzled. The guy couldn't stop mentioning some Sherlock Holmes here and some Watson there. After hearing it for a while, it almost made her want to fall asleep.

[Thank goodness my Heiji isn't like him,] she thought to herself.

Ran smiled in resignation. "Shinichi is like this. He's a fan of Sherlock Holmes."

"Don't tell me he's been talking about that the entire time..." Kazuha said, as if she had suddenly realized something.

"Yes, since the date started, it's been all about Sherlock Holmes."

Saying this, Ran also felt a little disappointed.

Kazuha stood there, mouth agape, staring at Ran in amazement. "Has he been talking about that Sherlock Holmes since the beginning of the date?"

Ran forced a smile and nodded slightly.

Kazuha was speechless. She could only take Ran's hand to offer some comfort. She couldn't even imagine what kind of torture it must have been.

Unaware of all this, Kudo Shinichi continued to talk non-stop to Heiji.

"If you want to know what's most amazing about Sherlock Holmes, it's when he first met his assistant Watson. With just a handshake, he knew that Watson had been in Afghanistan as a military doctor, just like that..."

Suddenly, he grabbed the hand of a girl who was ahead of them.

"Ah!"

The gesture from Kudo Shinichi startled the woman.

"You mean to say this lady must have practiced gymnastics, right?" Heiji said resignedly.

"Ah, how did you know?" Kudo Shinichi asked, confused.

"Because as we were walking, a gust of wind lifted this lady's skirt, revealing the calluses on her legs that are only formed by practicing gymnastics," Heiji said, shrugging.

"Wow, looks like Heiji is a bit more impressive than Shinichi, huh?" Ran joked from behind, as a way to vent her displeasure.

"Actually, I also saw it, but Hattori beat me to it," Kudo Shinichi said, annoyed.

He had indeed seen it, but the skirt had only lifted for an instant, less than a second in total. He hadn't expected Heiji's observational skills to be so sharp.

It was at this moment that Kudo Shinichi started to look at Heiji seriously, considering him a rival.

"Ahem, I think you should let go of the girl's hand now," Heiji reminded him.

"Ah, sorry, sorry," Kudo Shinichi apologized, embarrassed.

"It's fine," the girl said, walking away, clearly lost in thought.

"Shinichi, you didn't do that on purpose, did you?" Ran asked suspiciously.

"Silly, how could I have done it on purpose?" Kudo Shinichi responded, exasperated at Ran's suspicion.

Boom!

Suddenly, someone bumped into Kudo Shinichi.

"Hey, be more careful while walking."

Two men dressed in black gave him a look and walked off.

"There's a murderous aura. That man had an intense murderous aura," Kudo Shinichi thought, shivering, and looked at Heiji gravely. "Hey, Hattori, did you feel it? Those two aren't normal."

Heiji looked at the two men, and his gaze met one of theirs, but his expression was completely calm.

"I didn't see anything unusual. Maybe you were mistaken."

The two men were Gin and Vodka from the Black Organization. It was impossible for Heiji not to recognize them, but he had his own plans. Kudo Shinichi had to become Edogawa Conan; otherwise, how would the "Little Shinigami of Elementary School" gift awaken?

To remove his evil value, the plot in which Kudo Shinichi became Edogawa Conan could not be altered under any circumstances.

Kudo Shinichi said nothing. He was sure he hadn't been mistaken. It seemed that Heiji's observational ability was still a little lacking.

"Brother, it's Kudo Shinichi," said Vodka quietly.

"More than Kudo Shinichi, I'm more interested in that other high school student," said Gin indifferently, looking at Heiji with a slight air of seriousness.

"That student? He's just a brat," said Vodka disdainfully of Heiji, forgetting that Kudo Shinichi was also a high school student.

"Don't underestimate him. When our gazes crossed earlier, he didn't show the slightest trace of surprise. He's definitely not a simple character. During the operation later, be careful. Don't let him track us," said Gin coldly.

"Understood, brother," Vodka's heart shrank. Gin's gaze was as cold as ice, and he didn't dare disobey him, though he still didn't think the student was anything special.

"Heiji, there are empty seats over there."

"Since it's the first time I'm meeting Hattori, can I sit with him?" said Kudo Shinichi, wanting to talk to Heiji, and got into the car with him.

Heiji shrugged and turned to Kazuha. He hadn't expected Kudo Shinichi to do something like this.

"Sorry, Kazuha," Ran apologized.

"Don't worry about it. I'm sure Kudo has something to say to Heiji. Anyway, Heiji and I see each other every day, it's no big deal to lose this little time," said Kazuha generously.

"Thanks, Kazuha."

Ran, of course, knew that Kazuha was being considerate of her feelings. After all, when you're on a date with your boyfriend, the natural thing is to want to spend time with him. What Shinichi had done was rather inconsiderate.

"Do you know me?" Shinichi Kudo asked, looking at Kazuha with surprise.

"I don't know you," Kazuha replied firmly.

"Ahem, I'm Heiji Hattori from Osaka, and this is my girlfriend, Kazuha Toyama. By the way, I'm also a detective," Heiji said, standing up calmly.

"Detective? You're also a detective, like Shinichi?"

Undoubtedly, the young woman who had sat on Heiji's lap earlier was Ran Mouri. Just like in the anime, she had long hair that looked like a cloud, a beautiful and adorable face, a prominent bust, a tall, slender figure, and a pair of long, white, beautiful legs. Next to Kazuha, they were like spring orchids, each with their own charm, impossible to compare.

"Heiji Hattori, second-year student at Kaiho Academy in Osaka. The Kansai high school detective. I'm often compared to you, under the slogan 'Kudo in the East, Hattori in the West.' Your father is the head of the Osaka police, and you're an expert in kendo. Am I wrong?" Shinichi Kudo said, raising an eyebrow in a somewhat provocative tone.

"Wow, I didn't know you knew so much about me. That's right, it's me," Heiji smiled indifferently.

This guy...

Shinichi Kudo became a bit more serious inside. He had purposely emphasized that he was mentioned first, intending to provoke this high school detective who shared his fame, but he hadn't expected the other party to react so calmly.

"It seems I can't underestimate you at all."

"Same here."

They both laughed. Kazuha and Ran exchanged glances, both with a resigned expression.

Although they were laughing, Heiji didn't intend to get too close to Shinichi Kudo. In his previous life, he had been a killer, someone who took lives at will, and he naturally felt a slight aversion toward people brimming with a sense of justice.

Bad luck, Shinichi Kudo was precisely that type of person. However, his "Shinigami" attribute could be of use.

"Oh, so you're on your honeymoon!" Ran exclaimed, surprised and happy.

"Honeymoon? Heiji and I are just dating," Kazuha said shyly.

"What do you mean? Look at your red face!" Ran continued, teasing her.

"Don't talk about me. What about you and Kudo? Have you ever kissed?" Kazuha countered.

"Kissed?" Ran immediately blushed. She glanced at Shinichi Kudo, and seeing he wasn't paying attention, she felt a bit discouraged.

Shinichi Kudo wasn't interested in the girls' conversation at all. He kept talking to Heiji about various things, almost all related to cases.

He seemed particularly interested when he heard about the murder case that morning, and he asked Heiji to tell him the whole process.

Heiji told Shinichi Kudo all the clues and then went silent, leaving it to this deduction fanatic to figure out who the murderer was.

"Kazuha, we're out of drinks, please get me another one."

"Sure. Ran, wait for me, I'll be right back." Kazuha obediently ran off to buy the drinks.

"Hattori, although this might sound a bit sudden, you should really value Kazuha. She's a great girl," Ran told Heiji firmly.

"Hmm?" Heiji was a little surprised.

"Don't misunderstand me, I just think Kazuha is an amazing girl, and you should appreciate her," Ran realized she had been a bit blunt and quickly explained.

"Of course, I won't let Kazuha be sad. She'll become the happiest princess," Heiji said, a flash of tenderness in his eyes as he watched Kazuha approach.

How envious!

Seeing Heiji's gaze, Ran felt a little envious because she knew Shinichi would never look at her that way.

Unaccountably, she felt a little down.

Shinichi Kudo was still deep in thought, while Heiji, on the other hand, was chatting lively with the two girls. With his eloquence, he naturally made them laugh nonstop.

"Ah, I know! The murderer is Honda Kumaji, and the stain on the neck of the shirt was a mixture of potassium cyanide and melted water."

While the three were deep in conversation, Shinichi Kudo suddenly shouted, looking at Heiji with confidence.

What could be done?

Before this deduction fanatic, Heiji could only nod in resignation, having lost all interest in the conversation.

Kazuha looked at Shinichi Kudo with indifference, feeling a little lucky that her Heiji wasn't like that; otherwise, this date would be so boring.

"Heiji, let's ride the pendulum."

"Sure. Well, we're leaving now."

"Ran, I feel a bit sorry for you," Kazuha whispered to Ran's ear.

Watching the couple's figures walk away, embracing each other, Ran felt a mix of resignation and envy. She shot Shinichi Kudo a glare: "Shinichi, can't you just have fun with me?"

"But I'm having fun with you," Shinichi replied, completely confused by the scolding.

"Forget it, let's take a walk," said Ran, a little discouraged.

Shinichi, of course, noticed and, although he didn't understand what he had done wrong, kept apologizing.

On the pendulum ride, Kazuha hugged Heiji tightly, screaming at the top of her lungs between the whistle of the wind, filled with a mixture of excitement and fear.

"Idiot, if you're too scared to get on, why ask me to come with you?"

After getting off the pendulum ride, Kazuha's legs were shaking. She completely leaned on Heiji's body, letting him support her.

"Exactly because I'm scared, I ask you to come with me. If Heiji is with me, I'm not afraid of anything," Kazuha said sweetly.

"Idiot, in the future, measure your strength, don't act like a brave one."

Heiji was touched by her. In Kazuha's world, as long as he was present, he was her everything, and she had nothing to fear. That was a sign of how deeply she loved him.

"Okay. But I still want to ride the roller coaster," Kazuha said, looking at Heiji with expectation.

"The roller coaster, do you dare to ride it?" Heiji asked, looking at her skeptically.

"Of course I do."

"Then let's go. But don't regret it."

"I won't regret it."

The two figures, embraced, cast shadows on the ground, which grew longer and longer, until they merged into one.

"Ding... Congratulations to the host for successfully solving a Level C case. 10 evil points have been deducted." As soon as Honda Kumaji confessed, the mechanical voice of the system resonated.

"Only 10 points," Heiji grimaced. "Open the character attribute panel."

A virtual attribute panel appeared before Heiji's eyes, visible only to him.

Evil Value: -99985

"Ugh, when will this evil value end?" That blood-red number made him feel completely helpless.

Ding-dong! "Dear passengers, we have arrived at Beika station. Please exit through the right-hand door. We wish you a pleasant journey."

At that moment, the train stopped at the station. The police who were already waiting outside rushed in and took Honda Kumaji and Akagi Takeo's body.

"Ah, you're Heiji Hattori! I've heard that this case was solved thanks to you. You truly deserve to be the son of Superintendent Heizo Hattori, head of the Osaka Prefectural Police."

As soon as Heiji and Kazuha got off the train, a burly policeman approached them, full of praise.

"Are you Inspector Megure?"

Though he phrased it as a question, his tone was certain. After all, a character with such a classic appearance was instantly recognizable.

"That's right. I didn't expect young Hattori to visit Beika from Osaka. But if you hadn't come, this case wouldn't have been solved so quickly," Inspector Megure said enthusiastically.

"I came because Kazuha wanted to visit Beika, so I accompanied her."

"Oh, and this young lady is..." said Inspector Megure, looking at Kazuha.

"Hello, my name is Kazuha Toyama, I'm Heiji's girlfriend. Nice to meet you," Kazuha said naturally and gracefully.

"Oh, so you're a couple. You must be having a great time. Beika has many fun places to visit..."

"Inspector Megure..."

"Ah, I have to get back to work. In any case, thank you so much for today. When you have time, I'll invite you for tea."

"Heiji, who is he?" Kazuha asked curiously, looking at the back of Inspector Megure as he walked away.

"Inspector Juzo Megure, from the Third Violent Crimes Section of the First Investigation Division of the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department. He's an inspector with a strong sense of justice," Heiji smiled calmly.

It was their first time visiting Beika city, so everything was new to them. Without a fixed plan, they spent the morning strolling through the streets, eating and drinking.

On the terrace of a café, Heiji sat in a chair, exhausted, watching Kazuha, who was full of energy.

Women's constitution is really strange. When it comes to shopping, they're like monsters; it seems like they never get tired.

"Heiji, after shopping, let's go to Tropical Land amusement park, okay?" Kazuha said, looking at Heiji expectantly.

Heiji actually didn't want to, but the main purpose of the trip to Beika was to take Kazuha out to have fun, so refusing would go against his original intention.

"Okay, as you say."

Soft and fragrant lips landed on his. Mmm... in the end, it wasn't all bad.

Tropical Land amusement park. Since it was winter vacation, it was packed with people.

Kazuha dragged Heiji around between the crowds, trying almost every popular ride.

"Phew, I'm so tired. Heiji, shall we get something to drink?" she said.

It was already afternoon. After playing all day, Kazuha's cheeks were flushed; it was clear she was a bit tired.

"Idiot, we're not just here for one day. Was it necessary to push yourself this hard?" Heiji scolded her.

"What are you saying! It's my first date with Heiji, of course, I have to make the most of it before you suddenly run off to investigate a case!" Kazuha said, clinging tightly to Heiji's arm as if afraid he would escape.

Heiji sighed with resignation and let her hug him, thinking to himself: "Good thing I'm not Kudo Shinichi, because this girl couldn't stand such an endless wait; she's too clingy."

Since it was vacation, even though it was already afternoon, the cafés were crowded.

"Now what? This is the third one we've checked. How can there be so many people?"

Looking at the packed café, Kazuha became discouraged. It was very hard to find a seat and she was very hungry.

Heiji was also getting frustrated. He grabbed Kazuha and started walking between the tables, looking for a place where they could share a table with someone.

At that moment, a table became free.

Heiji's eyes lit up, and he pulled Kazuha to quickly move toward it.

At the same time, a couple appeared next to the vacant table.

"Shinichi, there's a seat, hurry!"

A clear, feminine voice was heard, and the girl rushed for the same seat Heiji was going for.

Bad luck. Heiji was one step faster and sat down first. The person who arrived a moment later landed directly on his lap.

The four of them froze for a moment. Two seconds later...

"Ah~~!! Pervert!"

A sharp scream sounded, and a white, slender hand flew towards him with great force.

Heiji's face changed. With lightning speed, he grabbed the hand and pressed a pressure point on her arm to nullify the force that sent shivers down his spine.

"Calm down, it was a misunderstanding, a misunderstanding."

The woman seemed to calm down. She quickly stood up and stood to the side, blushing. "Sorry, I was actually at fault too."

Heiji sighed in relief inside. The girl had a very good figure, but what surprised him most was the strength of that slap. It wasn't the strength that a normal woman should have... no, in fact, it surpassed that of many men.

"Heiji, are you okay?" Kazuha asked, reacting with concern.

"I'm fine."

"See? I told you not to rush. You look ridiculous, haha," the guy said, enjoying the situation.

"Shinichi..." the girl glared at the guy.

"Shinichi? The shinigami?"

Heiji looked at the guy in surprise. He was very handsome, with potential to be a "pretty boy." However, what was most impressive were his eyes: they were very self-assured!

"So, you're that Shinichi Kudo? You don't seem that impressive. My Heiji is more handsome."

Kazuha looked at Shinichi Kudo, made a face, and looked at him with disdain.

Heiji was very pleased with Kazuha's reaction. That's the reaction a girlfriend should have. As a competent girlfriend, you should always believe that your man is the best.

"First of all, the lights in car three were deliberately sabotaged, and the small lamp on Akagi's table is the evidence. Only if the lights were not working could the criminal plan be carried out. When the train entered the tunnel, in the complete darkness, Honda used the hidden murder weapon inside the pen's body to stab Akagi in the neck. As everyone knows, potassium cyanide is a lethal poison; once it enters the bloodstream, it can cause instant death. Once Akagi was dead, pouring the remaining potassium cyanide into the glass of water was a piece of cake, because Akagi was already dead and could not stop him..."

"One moment, please. How did Mr. Honda know that Mr. Akagi would definitely sit behind him?" asked the stewardess skeptically.

Tickets for this train do not have assigned seats; it was impossible to predict where Akagi would sit. And Honda Kumaji had been sitting in that spot from the beginning, without changing places.

"No, that's true. Mr. Akagi changed seats halfway through the journey, he sat there voluntarily," said Kazuha, surprised.

"If he sat there voluntarily, what does that have to do with Honda?" said Engo Masanami indifferently.

"Idiot, think about why Akagi moved voluntarily," Heiji snapped.

"The lamp! When the car went dark, he moved voluntarily for the lamp," Kazuha said aloud.

Heiji nodded with a satisfied smile: "Exactly, it was for the lamp. Normally, there are no lamps in the car; this lamp was attached to that table, and to see clearly in the dark, it was natural for Akagi to sit there."

"But that doesn't prove that the murderer is Honda. Besides, we don't even know what the murder weapon was," said Katsu Nanako resignedly.

"The murder weapon? If I'm not mistaken, the weapon was actually a needle of ice, with a wide head and a tip as fine as a pin. This needle of ice was mixed with a large amount of potassium cyanide."

The people present were stunned, with expressions of complete disbelief.

Honda Kumaji's face turned pale, his pupils contracted, and he looked at Heiji in disbelief.

How does this kid know that? Impossible, he must be guessing.

"But, Mr. Heiji, how did you know?" asked the stewardess curiously.

"Akagi's shirt collar was wet, and the fog formed on the mirror is the proof," Heiji explained.

Everyone suddenly understood. So that was the reason Heiji had used the mirror earlier.

"How ridiculous. Even if it's true, as you say, that the murder weapon was a needle of ice with that shape, how was I supposed to bring it onto the train? As you know, without refrigeration, it would have evaporated quickly," said Honda Kumaji with a cold smile.

"Oh, that's why I said the pen's body is the evidence," Heiji said confidently.

Boom!

Honda Kumaji's heart skipped a beat, and he looked at Heiji with a trace of panic.

Why does this kid look so confident? Has he really figured out my method?

"Perhaps many people don't know, but wrapping ice in dry cotton helps preserve it, preventing as much evaporation as possible. And your method must have been to completely empty the pen and then insert the ice needle wrapped in cotton inside. Of course, that needle was made from a frozen mixture of potassium cyanide and water. Once inside, you extracted the air to create a vacuum state, which would prevent the ice needle from melting quickly for a while. And the water droplets inside the pen's body are the result of the needle's evaporation, and there is still a faint trace of almond smell. That's the proof!"

The car fell silent. Heiji's deduction was truly overwhelming.

Honda Kumaji's expression froze completely, and a deep sense of panic overtook his gaze.

How does this kid know all this? My plan was perfect, why does he know all these details, as if he saw it with his own eyes? Impossible, it's impossible.

"But, Mr. Heiji, the water droplets inside the pen have already disappeared," Katsu Nanako whispered.

Suddenly, Honda Kumaji, like a drowning man clinging to a piece of wood, regained his confidence: "That can't be proof. Also, now that I remember, I washed this pen last night, those must be water droplets left from then. As for the almond smell, you must have made a mistake."

"It seems you're planning to deny your guilt until the end, right?" Heiji still had the upper hand.

"I'm not the murderer, why would I confess?" said Honda Kumaji fiercely.

"The pen's body is just one of the pieces of evidence, not the decisive one. The definitive proof is here."

Heiji picked up the tissue pack, opened it, and took out the tissues one by one.

Suddenly, a piece of paper flew out and landed on the table, covered in text.

"This must be the paper Akagi was reading earlier. I'm sure you can find his fingerprints on it. The fact that the paper Akagi had right before he died is now in your possession is already enough proof that you're the murderer. But there's one more piece of evidence that you won't be able to refute. And it is..."

Heiji pulled a wet cotton ball out of the tissue pack. Instantly, the people present covered their noses. A strong smell of almonds!!!

Seeing that cotton ball, Honda Kumaji's face completely changed, and his gaze filled with hopelessness.

"This must be the cotton you used to preserve the ice needle, right? At this point, do you still think you can deny it?" Heiji said confidently.

Honda Kumaji clenched his fists tightly, and after a long while, relaxed them in a gesture of defeat.

"You really live up to your name, Hattori. I admit your deductive ability. That's right, I killed Akagi. Who told him to discover that I was embezzling funds by taking advantage of my position as chief and even get proof? To rid myself of his threats, I decided to kill him and get rid of the problem once and for all. I thought my plan was perfect, but unfortunately, I didn't count on you being here," said Honda Kumaji, completely dejected.

"Humans have flaws, only machines can be perfect. And before a Machinist, no crime can remain hidden."

An aura of imposing confidence emanated from Heiji's body.

"When did I say that the fingerprint on the glass was the killer's?" Heiji said calmly.

"What?" Honda Kumaji's face changed, and he was left with his mouth open.

"Then why did Heiji have them compare the fingerprints?" Kazuha asked curiously.

"Comparing the fingerprints was just a means to achieve my goal. Besides, I already knew from the beginning whose fingerprint it was," Heiji said with confidence.

"Was it my fingerprint?" whispered the steward from the side.

"Correct, it was the stewardess's fingerprint, but that doesn't matter anymore. Mr. Honda, you'd better confess peacefully."

Heiji looked at Honda Kumaji with certainty.

"This... you must be wrong. How could I have killed Akagi? It's impossible," Honda Kumaji said, waving his hands repeatedly, with an innocent smile.

"Then can you explain what that smell on your hand is?"

"Smell?"

Honda Kumaji sniffed his hand. His pupils contracted, and his face instantly turned pale.

"Did you notice that, despite your meticulous plan, you missed a detail, and now the smell of almonds is lingering on your hand?" Heiji said calmly.

"That must be... it must be..."

"It must be what? You didn't touch the corpse at any moment. Did potassium cyanide fly to your hand on its own?" Heiji said with a cold smile.

Honda Kumaji's face changed repeatedly until it finally became cold: "Since you're saying I'm the killer, then tell me how I killed him. As soon as I moved, Akagi would have noticed instantly. I had no chance to put the poison in the glass of water."

"That's true, Heiji. He was sitting there. If he had extended his arm to the glass, the movement would have been too large and surely they would have discovered it," Kazuha whispered beside him.

"Fool, did I say that Akagi died from drinking the water from the glass?" Heiji said while pinching Kazuha's pretty nose.

"What? Are you saying Akagi wasn't poisoned?"

The people present stared at Heiji in astonishment, completely confused.

From the beginning, everyone had assumed that Akagi had died from drinking the water from the glass. They hadn't expected such a drastic twist that would catch everyone by surprise.

Honda Kumaji was horrified inside, staring at Heiji in complete disbelief.

"Mr. Heiji, how did this passenger die?" asked the stewardess, who just wanted Heiji to solve the case once and for all.

"Look, here's a wound the size of a pin. This is the real cause of Akagi's death."

Heiji lifted Akagi's shirt collar, revealing the small, bleeding wound.

"I understand now! You mean Honda used a needle to inject potassium cyanide into Akagi's neck and kill him?" exclaimed Engo Masanami.

"Oh, in that case, feel free to search me. Let's see if you find a needle or something that looks like a needle."

"Perfect. Since you say so, I will proceed to search you."

"Go ahead." A disdainful smile briefly crossed Honda Kumaji's lips.

Quickly, all of Honda Kumaji's belongings were placed on another table. Heiji wouldn't allow anyone to contaminate the crime scene.

A pen, a pack of tissues, a wallet, a bunch of keys, and a nail clipper.

That was all Honda Kumaji had on him.

"See? I don't have anything resembling a needle. Of course, if you think you can kill someone with a pen, then there's nothing more I can say," Honda Kumaji said confidently.

"And who says a pen can't kill?"

Heiji's words caused a great stir among the people present, who looked at him horrified.

"Detective, don't tell me Akagi died from bleeding out from that wound! What kind of joke is this?" Honda Kumaji shouted.

The others didn't say anything, but their expressions said it all: this was simply impossible.

"Heiji~~," Kazuha couldn't help but hug Heiji, somewhat worried.

Heiji smiled confidently, unscrewed the pen, and to everyone's surprise, there was neither ink nor a cartridge inside.

"What's going on? Why doesn't it have a cartridge or ink?" Kazuha asked, surprised.

"Nothing strange about it. This pen has a special meaning for me, sentimental value. It's not for writing," Honda Kumaji said indifferently.

Heiji ignored him. He looked inside the pen and saw small drops of water on the inner wall and a faint smell. This discovery completely validated his theory.

Ding-dong! "Dear passengers, we would like to inform you that we will arrive at Beika Station in five minutes. Please make sure to take all your carry-on luggage. The exit will be through the right-side door. We wish you a pleasant journey."

Silence took over carriage number three.

"Well, we're almost at the station, so I'm not going to keep playing detective with you," Honda Kumaji tried to gather his things, but suddenly, a hand stopped him.

"If I let you collect the evidence so easily, wouldn't I look useless?" Heiji said calmly.

"What? Did you say the evidence? Is there evidence among these things?" exclaimed Katsu Nanako, surprised.

"Hey, hey, you don't really think this pen can kill someone, do you?" said Engo Masanami skeptically.

"The body of the pen is the evidence, but it's not the murder weapon. It's the container that held it. The real murder weapon is already gone."

"Hahaha! You keep impressing me more and more. The famous Hattori from Kansai? Seems like your fame is undeserved. The murder weapon is gone; do you think you can blame the murder on me by force?" Honda Kumaji laughed out loud.

"Don't rush, let me finish talking first."

Heiji let go of Honda Kumaji's hand, put his hands in his pockets, and leaned against the back of the train seat.

"Oh, there it is. Heiji's coolest deduction pose," Kazuha said with stars in her eyes.

What Honda Kumaji said was true. He was sitting behind Akagi Takeo, and trying to pour cyanide into the glass from behind without being discovered was indeed impossible.

However, is it really like that?

Heiji lowered his head, thoughtful. This case had four major points of doubt.

First: if cyanide had been poured into the glass of water, some water would have splashed around the glass. But it is clear that the table is clean, and there is no sign it was wiped down.

Second: why does the collar of the deceased's shirt have a wet stain, and why is the almond smell much stronger there than in the glass?

Third: what does that needle mark on the deceased's neck mean, and what is its connection to the case?

Fourth: what was the content of the paper the deceased was reading? Has it already been destroyed?

Connecting all these doubts, it was clear that the case was much more complex than it appeared at first glance.

"Damn, these Level C cases are not easy at all."

The interrogation was over. Although Heiji had a theory, the clues he had found weren't enough to confirm it.

"Hey, detective, you'd better solve the case quickly. The next station is my destination, and I have an interview at the North Pole Ice Sculpture Company. Don't ruin it for me," said Engo Masanami, annoyed.

"Yes, I also have to go to work," added Honda Kumaji.

"Are you also getting off at Beika Station? We are too!" said Kazuha, happily.

Ice sculpture arts?

Ice?

Ice!!!!!

Heiji had a sudden revelation, and a sharp gleam crossed his eyes.

"Mr. Engo, are you into ice sculpture?"

"That's right. Not just me, Honda and the deceased Akagi also worked in it. In fact, we had been working together for three years. If it weren't for that damn Akagi... maybe I wouldn't have left the South Pole Ice Sculpture Arts," said Engo Masanami.

Heiji nodded, approached the deceased's body, and lifted the collar of his shirt again. "Kazuha, give me your mirror."

Kazuha took a small mirror out of her purse and handed it to him.

He placed the mirror inside the collar of the shirt, and slowly, the surface of the mirror began to fog up with a fine layer of vapor.

Just as he thought.

A confident smile appeared at the corner of Heiji's lips. So, this was the method used for the murder. This way, it was truly stealthy and imperceptible, without even leaving fingerprints.

What a coincidence. In his past life as a machinist, he had also used a similar method to kill a business tycoon without leaving a trace. He didn't expect someone to try to boast of their skills right in front of him.

If this method was used, then that object must be in their possession.

"Heiji, what are you doing?" asked Kazuha, curious.

"Solving the case."

A confident smile formed on Heiji's lips. If this was the technique, then the killer was him. However, he still needed one final confirmation.

"Wow, there's a fingerprint on the glass," Heiji said suddenly, feigning surprise as he stared at the glass.

"What?"

The three of them jolted and looked at the glass. Indeed, there was a barely visible fingerprint that would go unnoticed if one didn't pay attention.

"Could it be Akagi's fingerprint?" whispered Katsu Nanako.

"I've already compared it. It's not the deceased's fingerprint. To confirm, come closer and compare yours as well," said Heiji with a half-smile.

"Damn it! I didn't kill him! Why should I listen to you?" snorted Engo Masanami.

"Are you sure you don't want to obey?" Heiji's eyes glowed with a cold light that scared Engo Masanami, making him recall the scene before getting on the train.

"Hmph, since I didn't kill him, I have nothing to fear."

He was still playing tough.

"Then, please, place your hand over the glass without touching it, following the shape of the fingerprint. Remember, do not touch it, otherwise, if you destroy the evidence, I'll consider you the culprit," said Heiji seriously.

"Ugh, what a nuisance."

Engo Masanami extended his hand and held it above the glass. Heiji slightly tilted his head and imperceptibly inhaled the smell.

"It's not."

"Hmph, of course not. I'm innocent, how could I...?"

Suddenly, Engo Masanami fell silent and stepped aside.

Heiji withdrew his cold gaze and looked at Katsu Nanako and Honda Kumaji.

"I'll go first," said Honda Kumaji, approaching confidently and repeating the same steps.

"This smell..."

Heiji raised an eyebrow. The culprit was already evident.

"Well, it seems it's not my fingerprint," Honda Kumaji said, laughing loudly.

"Then... I'll go," said Katsu Nanako, approaching and making the gesture to compare the fingerprint.

"No need. I already know who the killer is," said Heiji, hands in his pockets, full of confidence.

"Ah, it wasn't me, it wasn't me! I can compare the fingerprint!"

Katsu Nanako turned pale with fear, thinking that Heiji was referring to her.

"So, it was you who killed him. It seems you still hated him a lot, even though Akagi deserved it," said Engo Masanami, enjoying the misfortune of others.

"I didn't do it, I didn't do it!" sobbed Katsu Nanako.

"Then I'll call the police right away," said Honda Kumaji, pulling out his phone to dial.

"Of course, we need to call the police. However, the person they're going to arrest isn't Miss Nanako, but you, Mr. Honda Kumaji."

"What?"

Everyone in the train car was stunned, staring at Heiji in utter disbelief.

"What... what kind of joke is this? I was sitting back to back with Akagi, with two seats in between us. And most importantly, if I had wanted to poison his glass, I would have been discovered instantly. Also, the fingerprint on the glass isn't mine, that proves I'm not the killer!" Honda Kumaji defended himself hastily.
