Heiji picked up the glass of water from the table and sniffed it. To his surprise, the water only had a faint and very subtle trace of almond odor. Also, he realized that something was missing from the table.

After searching carefully, Heiji could not find that object. He looked up at the three people in the wagon, and a decision had already formed in his mind.

"Well? Have you discovered anything?" asked the middle-aged man with curiosity.

"This is a murder case," said Heiji.

The tension in the air dissipated suddenly, and everyone looked at Heiji with disdain. Anyone could see that; was it necessary to point it out?

"It seems the Heiji Hattori from Kansai isn't all that," said Engo Masanami with contempt.

Heiji smiled confidently, and a sharp gleam flashed in his eyes.

"It seems you haven't understood what I mean. The implication of 'this is a murder case' is that... the murderer is one of the people here."

What?

The people present felt a knot in their stomach, and surprise reflected in their eyes.

"Does this mean that I, too, am a suspect of murder?" asked the steward, terrified.

"That possibility cannot be ruled out," said Heiji.

"But... but I have no reason to kill! Why would I want to kill him?" The steward was about to cry.

"Exactly, why would we want to kill Akagi Takeo?" defended the middle-aged man.

"That's right, you shouldn't accuse people lightly," added the woman.

"That kind of person, arrogant and rude, surely has many enemies. Why do you think we would be the ones to kill him?" snorted Engo Masanami.

Heiji listened to their explanations without flinching, and only when they finished speaking did he begin to explain.

"Before I present my arguments, I'd like to ask you something, sir."

Heiji looked at the middle-aged man.

"Ask me? Are you saying I'm the murderer?" shouted the man.

"Don't react like that. I just want to understand some basic details," said Heiji calmly.

"I won't answer your questions; you're making me look like the murderer," said the man coldly.

"Not answering is admitting you have something to hide. And if you have something to hide, it proves you have a motive to kill that you don't dare to reveal. Also, you knew the deceased, right?"

Although it was a question, Heiji's tone was one of complete certainty.

"You..."

The middle-aged man lowered his head. "My name is Honda Kumaji, and I was a coworker of Akagi Takeo in the same company. Oh, by the way, Engo Masanami was also a coworker."

"Don't say that, Mr. Honda. Since yesterday, I'm no longer your employee, nor do I work at that company," said Engo Masanami with a mocking smile.

Honda Kumaji ignored Engo Masanami and instead looked at Heiji with doubt. "How did you know I knew Akagi?"

Heiji smiled confidently. "You hadn't exchanged a word before, yet you were able to immediately say the name of the deceased. It's clear you already knew him."

Honda Kumaji froze and then smiled bitterly. "You really live up to your reputation as a great high school detective. Your observational skills are impressive."

"So, can you answer my questions now?" asked Heiji.

"Ask. Anyway, I didn't kill him, ask whatever you want," said Honda Kumaji confidently.

"I don't mind," shrugged Engo Masanami.

"I... I will cooperate actively too," said the woman softly.

"Good, then I'll start with you, miss. What's your name and did you know the deceased?"

"My name is Katsu Nanako, I'm the owner of an ice cream shop, and yes, I knew Mr. Akagi," said Katsu Nanako quietly.

"I think it was more than just an acquaintance, right? That Akagi was your ex-boyfriend, wasn't he? And I heard that he was the one who dumped you," mocked Engo Masanami from the side.

"Oh, in that case, she would have a motive to kill Akagi," added Honda Kumaji, fueling the fire.

"That's not true, that's not true! It's true that I was his girlfriend, but I was the one who broke up with him. And I didn't kill him," said Katsu Nanako, panicking.

"Did he treat you badly?" asked Kazuha curiously.

"He often borrowed money from me, and it was always significant amounts. At first, I didn't think much of it, but after it happened over and over, I finally couldn't take it anymore and asked for an explanation. It turned out he only approached me for my money. I couldn't stand it anymore and broke up with him," said Katsu Nanako sadly.

"And as a result, even after breaking up, he continued to harass you. You couldn't take it anymore and killed him, right?" said Engo Masanami with a cold smile.

"No, I didn't do it!" Katsu Nanako defended herself, shouting.

"The motive makes sense," agreed Honda Kumaji.

Heiji lowered his head and thought for a moment, then looked at Katsu Nanako. "When we entered the tunnel, why did you get up from your seat? Although the wagon was very dark, the perfume you left when passing by is the same one you're wearing. It must have been you."

Katsu Nanako froze.

"I just had a stomach ache, I went to the bathroom, that's all."

"Really went to the bathroom? Or maybe you took the opportunity to put potassium cyanide in Akagi's glass of water?" said Engo Masanami sarcastically.

Put?

Heiji's eyes lit up. He looked back at the table: the glass of water still had more than half left, and there were no splashes around it. Relating that to the needle mark on the deceased's neck and the damp stain on his shirt, the truth was getting closer.

"And you, Mr. Engo?"

"Me? I was sitting in the seat across from Akagi. If I had put poison in his glass, wouldn't he have noticed?" replied Engo Masanami with a cold smile.

Anyone who's traveled by train knows that seats are usually arranged in pairs facing each other. Engo Masanami's position was separated by at least two seats, and in order to put poison in the glass of water, he would have had to pass over them. Doing that without making any noise is very difficult.

"It was very dark, and the two seats are close together. That is, if you had chosen the right moment, it wouldn't have been impossible to pass over the seat and put the potassium cyanide in the glass," said Honda Kumaji.

"You... But why would I want to kill him?! I have no motive!" Engo Masanami said, exasperated.

"The deceased probably often mistreated you, or insulted you frequently."

Remembering the scene before getting on the train, it was easy for Heiji to find a motive. Engo Masanami didn't say anything, it was clear that he had hit the mark.

"Those two have a motive, but I don't. After all, my relationship with Akagi was quite good. Besides, I was sitting right behind him, it was impossible to put poison in his glass of water. Because as soon as I moved, he would have noticed," said Honda Kumaji confidently.

At that moment, the train passed through a short tunnel, and the car plunged into complete darkness; the lights did not turn on.

Total darkness!

"What's going on? Flight attendant, flight attendant...!"

Shouted Akagi Takeo. He had been reading something, and the sudden darkness bothered him greatly.

A flight attendant in uniform entered the car and bowed to Akagi Takeo: "Sir, do you need anything?"

"Your lights are not working, fix them immediately."

The flight attendant tried several times, but all the lights in car three were broken. Since the train was already moving, it was impossible to repair them, so he could only apologize repeatedly.

Akagi Takeo, muttering under his breath, looked around and headed directly to a seat where there was a small lamp.

Heiji looked at the little lamp curiously. It was impossible for a train to be equipped with lamps, meaning someone had placed it there on purpose.

The power of the lamp was too weak; it could only illuminate a very small area.

Akagi Takeo lowered his head to look at the paper in his hands. From Heiji's perspective, he could only make out the dense words covering it, but the content was a mystery.

The car fell silent again.

Surely, Kazuha had woken up very early to prepare the bento. After eating, she leaned on Heiji's shoulder and fell into a deep sleep.

Sensing Kazuha's faint body fragrance, Heiji, with nothing to do, decided to close his eyes and rest as well.

The train entered a tunnel once more.

This tunnel was much longer than the previous one, and the car suddenly plunged into darkness.

"Baka!"

In the darkness, Akagi Takeo's angry insult echoed, followed by the sound of a button, obviously trying to turn on the little lamp.

Pff~

Suddenly, an extremely subtle sound was heard in the darkness.

At the same time, Heiji felt someone rush past him.

Soon after, the train exited the tunnel, and the car was lit up again.

"Ladies and gentlemen, to compensate for the inconvenience, the train manager has decided to offer you a free bento meal." The flight attendant entered, pushing a service cart, and began handing out bentos to the few people in car three.

"Thank you."

Heiji accepted two bentos. Since they were free, there was no reason not to eat them.

"Sir, sir, ah...!"

When touched by the flight attendant, Akagi Takeo collapsed in the seat, his face pale and completely motionless.

"Heiji, what happened?" Kazuha woke up from the commotion.

"It looks like someone fainted... no, wait, it smells like almonds."

Ding-dong!

"A C-Level murder case has been detected. The host is requested to solve the case and find the culprit before the train reaches the next station. Otherwise, you will not receive the corresponding evil value."

I knew it!

The system notification confirmed Heiji's premonition: that guy was dead.

"What happened to him?" The middle-aged man wanted to approach and check.

"Nobody move! He's dead. You can't alter the crime scene."

A lazy voice, yet full of unquestionable authority, echoed.

"Dead? Call the police!" The middle-aged man stopped dead in his tracks...

"Dead? Doesn't look like it." The woman, who had just come out of the bathroom, looked at Akagi Takeo with skepticism. He seemed to just be asleep.

"Dead?" Engo Masanami was stunned for a moment, then a satisfied smile appeared on his face.

Heiji observed the expressions of the three, and although he had a general idea, he needed to examine the body to be sure.

"Dead? What do you mean dead? Heiji, call an ambulance!" Kazuha screamed.

"He's really dead. You should smell the almond scent in the air. It's the smell of potassium cyanide evaporating."

Heiji approached, holding Kazuha's hand, with a serene expression.

"Potassium cyanide? It's a very potent poison, but it needs to dissolve in water. Does this mean it was from that glass of water?" said the middle-aged man, looking at the glass in front of Akagi Takeo.

After the man's analysis, everyone focused on the glass of water.

Heiji did too, but he was not influenced by the man. He carefully examined the surroundings of Akagi Takeo and the body itself.

Suddenly!

He noticed that the collar of Akagi Takeo's shirt seemed to be damp.

"Kazuha, the gloves."

"Here, Heiji."

Kazuha quickly pulled a pair of white rubber gloves from her bag. She had become Heiji's assistant during investigations, and in her bag, along with money, documents, and some cosmetics, she carried a few small essentials for solving cases.

After putting on the gloves, Heiji prepared to examine Akagi Takeo's body.

However, the middle-aged man stopped him.

"Wait. You told us not to approach the body, so you can't get any closer either."

Heiji looked at the man: "I told you not to approach because you might contaminate the crime scene."

"Well, you could contaminate it too," replied the man with a cold smile.

"Heiji is not as clumsy as you all. He's very good at solving cases."

Hearing someone doubt Heiji, Kazuha became upset and, holding her boyfriend's arm, defended him proudly.

"Solving cases? Is he a cop?" the woman asked with curiosity.

"No, Heiji is a detective. A great detective!" Kazuha exclaimed, full of pride.

"A detective?"

The three were surprised.

"Let me introduce myself. My name is Heiji Hattori, and I am a detective," Heiji said calmly.

"Heiji Hattori! Are you the famous high school detective from Kansai?" exclaimed the flight attendant, surprised.

Upon hearing that Heiji seemed very famous, the expressions of the three suspects subtly changed.

"Then, may I pass?"

The middle-aged man quickly stepped aside. If he was a detective, there was no reason to stop him anymore.

The closer Heiji got to Akagi Takeo's body, the stronger the almond smell became.

Heiji carefully examined the collar of Akagi Takeo's shirt. He had barely lifted it slightly when a very strong almond scent hit his nose.

Although it was overpowering, Heiji made a new discovery.

Just above the collar of the shirt, on Akagi Takeo's neck, there was a tiny wound, like a needle prick, impossible to see unless one looked closely.

What does this wound mean?

Heiji stood still, lost in thought. What seemed like a simple case had now become confusing and full of doubts because of that wound.

Smack!

"Yes, yes."

"Your seats are in car number three. I wish you a pleasant trip."

"Car three, car three... here it is! Heiji, we... ouch!"

Kazuha was looking for the door to car three with the tickets in hand. Just as she found it and was about to tell Heiji, someone bumped into her.

"Sorry."

A woman, looking hurried, only turned to apologize to Kazuha before running toward the inside of the car.

"Well..." Kazuha muttered, irritated.

"Young people today... always in such a hurry." A middle-aged man, about fifty years old, shook his head and entered after her.

"Make way, make way!"

A burly man with a rough face was moving forward like a bulldozer, pushing everything aside. He was about to crash into Kazuha.

Suddenly, a hand grabbed the burly man's arm tightly.

"Ah!" The man let out a cry of pain.

"It's better to be a little kinder to girls," Heiji said calmly.

"You... let go of me, I won't do it again," the burly man said in a pained voice. He didn't expect a simple high school student to have such strength in his hand.

It wasn't that Heiji had a lot of strength, but rather that the place he had grabbed was precisely a pain point on the man's arm.

Knowing the weak points of the human body was an indispensable condition and an essential skill to be a Machinist.

"Look at you, big and strong, and getting intimidated by a high school student. What a useless guy."

An even bigger man looked at the other with disdain and mocked him.

"Akagi Takeo, don't be so arrogant!"

The first man rubbed his arm and stared at the one called Akagi Takeo, his eyes full of rage.

"Engo Masanami, you're nothing but a useless guy. And a useless guy dares to shout at me? Get out!" Akagi Takeo shoved Engo Masanami and entered car three.

Engo Masanami clenched his fists so tightly that his veins stood out. After a while, he managed to calm down and also entered car three. However, one of his gestures caught Heiji's attention.

It seemed that what he was carrying inside his clothes was very important.

"Heiji, let's go in," Kazuha said, pulling him to enter the car.

Since it was morning and also the weekend, there weren't many people in the car.

The hurried woman, the middle-aged man, Engo Masanami, the arrogant Akagi Takeo, and then Heiji and Kazuha.

Kazuha made Heiji sit, took two bentos from her backpack, and sweetly opened her boyfriend's bento and handed it to him.

"Heiji, breakfast."

Heiji ate the bento that Kazuha had lovingly prepared. He had to admit that the girl cooked very well, it really opened up his appetite.

Seeing Heiji devour the food, Kazuha felt a great sweetness in her heart and ate her own portion in small bites, completely satisfied.

However, seeing Kazuha's figure moving from side to side, her slender silhouette, her breasts gently shaking with her movement, and her firm, rounded backside, a flash of desire and a touch of tenderness crossed his eyes.

Maybe, having a real girlfriend wouldn't be so bad.

"Done, it's finally all cleaned up."

Thanks to Kazuha's effort, the room, which had been chaotic, was now neat and tidy. The books on the shelf were aligned, the things on the desk were in their place, and the shoes on the floor were well arranged.

After having been bent over for so long, Kazuha straightened up to stretch her muscles.

Suddenly, a pair of hands wrapped around her delicate waist, and with a pull, she was abruptly drawn into Heiji's embrace.

"Heiji?"

Kazuha lifted her head in surprise, only to be met with a mouth that lunged toward hers.

Mmm~

When their lips met, Kazuha's eyes opened wide. However, she soon lost herself in Heiji's expert technique.

Much later, Kazuha shyly leaned against Heiji's chest, her face completely flushed.

"You're already my woman. From now on, I don't want you thinking about any other handsome guys, understood?"

Although he hadn't really "taken" Kazuha yet, Heiji already considered her his woman, and he wouldn't allow her to chase after celebrities or get close to other men.

Kazuha lifted her head and gave him a reproachful look, but didn't pull away from his embrace.

"Heiji, actually... I've liked you for a long time. That was my first kiss."

A quiet confession, the reward for the longest wait.

Heiji couldn't help but hug the girl tighter. Though, at this moment, she wasn't in love with him, but with the other guy, he would make this girl fall in love with the Heiji of now.

After the confession, it was clear that Kazuha still didn't feel entirely comfortable, squirming shyly in Heiji's arms.

Heiji didn't mind. He hugged her, sat with her on the bed, rested his chin on her shoulder, and stayed silent.

At first, Kazuha felt strange, but little by little, her body relaxed, and she snuggled into Heiji's embrace, savoring the taste of her first love.

Since the confession, Kazuha's visits to Heiji's house skyrocketed. After all, they were childhood friends, and besides, Shizuka Hattori was very fond of the girl and would love to have her as a daughter-in-law.

So, she simply turned a blind eye.

Winter break was approaching, so both had plenty of free time.

In Heiji's small room, for him, Kazuha's body no longer held any secrets. Except for the last step, they had done everything that could be done.

Why not take the last step? Because Kazuha still had to go to school.

It would have to wait at least until summer vacation, right?

"Heiji, look, it seems like Shinichi Kudo, the one from Kanto, has solved another case."

Kazuha, wearing a loose T-shirt of Heiji's that revealed the trembling of her breasts with every movement, had her eyes fixed on the computer.

On the screen, the character who had recently been solving case after case appeared: the famous high school detective, Shinichi Kudo.

"No matter how difficult the case is, as long as it's a case, for me, the truth is always just one."

Heiji, who was doing push-ups, smiled slightly when he heard it. That was because he hadn't come across him yet; otherwise, he would make Shinichi Kudo doubt his own existence in a matter of minutes.

If he wanted, in a murder case, he could create several different culprits.

"Bah, so boring. They say Shinichi Kudo is the most incredible high school detective in Japan. For me, Heiji is the best."

Kazuha turned off the computer, annoyed.

During this time, Heiji had also come across several cases and solved them easily. And Kazuha had been by his side, so, for her, her boyfriend was the best.

Heiji stood up, took the towel Kazuha offered him, and smiled with disdain. "The media always goes with the flow. If I took it seriously, Shinichi Kudo wouldn't stand a chance."

Although he had solved several cases recently, all were level D cases, the most common ones. A level D case equaled one point of evil, which was a drop in the ocean compared to his enormous negative evil value.

At this point, Heiji needed to explain the levels of the cases. There were a total of five categories: S, A, B, C, and D.

A level S case equaled 1000 evil points.

A level A case equaled 500 evil points.

A level B case equaled 100 evil points.

A level C case equaled 10 evil points.

A level D case equaled 1 evil point.

I don't know if it sounds like a scam to you, but Heiji certainly thought it was, a heavenly scam, a cosmic scam. But there was nothing to be done, it was the disaster he had created, and only he could bear the consequences.

The sky was a deep blue, with white, pure clouds drifting slowly. Occasionally, one or two birds flew by, leaving behind a couple of sharp chirps.

On the grassy slope of a park, a young man in a baseball cap lay on his back, a blade of grass in his mouth and a look of helplessness in his dark, shining eyes.

His name was Ryūji... well, it used to be Ryūji, but now it was Heiji Hattori.

In his previous life, as a Machinist, his name was known to everyone in the underground world. The people who died at his hands weren't a thousand, but eight hundred.

All the people he killed seemed to have died by suicide or accident, without the slightest trace of human intervention, undetectable even with high-tech methods.

In the underground world, there was a saying: "It's better to offend Yama, the king of hell, than to offend a Machinist, especially Ryūji."

"Machinist" was not a profession like machine repair, but a special type of assassin.

To kill without leaving a trace. If someone wanted someone to die by accident, suicide, or sudden death, a Machinist could make it happen, without leaving a single piece of evidence.

Machinists were the elite in the assassin world, extremely rare, and Ryūji was the strongest of them all.

In that world, he had created the myth of eliminating ten elite Machinists by himself. If it hadn't been for his manager being driven by greed and betraying him, no one would have known about that incident.

Until now, he couldn't understand why that manager had betrayed him. It wasn't like he paid him poorly—an annual salary of ten million dollars was more than enough.

If he had known that someone had offered a hundred million dollars for information about him and a billion for his life, maybe he wouldn't have overthought it so much.

But he no longer had to worry about that. One day, while scouting the terrain, a thunderclap rang out from the sky, and when he woke up, he had crossed into this world, the world of Conan.

"How could I have fallen right onto Heiji Hattori...?" he sighed once more.

It wasn't a soul transmigration. It was that, upon crossing, he accidentally killed Heiji Hattori, who had been climbing a mountain. Coincidentally, he and Heiji Hattori looked very similar—his skin was just a little lighter, but it was impossible to tell if he was the real one.

Sharp, lively eyes, a handsome and determined face, a height of one seventy-eight, and that characteristic baseball cap...

He had no choice. To avoid unnecessary trouble and completely erase all traces of the original Heiji Hattori, a new Heiji Hattori appeared before everyone who knew him.

For a Machinist, the most basic skill is to integrate perfectly into any identity without being discovered. As the best Machinist he was, it didn't take him even a day to become Heiji Hattori.

"Heiji, hiding here again. It took me a while to find you."

A clear voice, tinged with a hint of complaint, came along with a faint, pleasant fragrance.

Heiji Hattori sighed softly, and after glancing at the beautiful young woman sitting beside him, he showed an impatient expression.

"Hey, Kazuha, why are you always following me? Can't you give me some personal space?"

Kazuha Toyama gave Heiji Hattori a reproachful look, hugged her knees, and watched him sneakily.

"It's not that I want to follow you all the time. It was Aunt Shizuka, she's afraid you'll get into trouble and asked me to watch over you."

Heiji Hattori responded with an "oh," but his skeptical tone made Kazuha blush slightly, as if he had guessed her true intentions.

"You... Aunt Shizuka told me to call you to come eat."

Kazuha was a little nervous.

"Ah, that. Let's go, I was just starting to get hungry." Heiji stood up from the grass. As for his parents in this world, he didn't feel much aversion toward them yet.

"Wait..."

Small hands suddenly started patting all over his body.

"Look at you, you have bits of grass all over your back, and you didn't even brush them off."

Heiji looked at Kazuha, who was slightly leaning toward him, with a tender expression he rarely saw in his previous world.

In that world, he had countless beautiful women, but it was all a farce. After all, an assassin cannot have emotions. Once a bond is created, the assassin is finished.

However, arriving in this world, where no one knew him, maybe he could experience that kind of emotion.

Besides, he could no longer kill at will.

In his previous world, his invincibility was because he possessed a mysterious system.

The Evil Value System!

This system was different from the ones in other novels; it didn't assign missions or offer rewards. It only had two functions: one was to record the host's evil value, and the other was to erase all traces of the host at the crime scene.

The reason Heiji became the most prominent Machinist in his previous life was that every time he killed someone, not the slightest trace could be found at the scene, not even a hint.

It was what is known as the perfect crime, or even the impossible crime.

However, Heiji knew he had been deceived. After killing countless people, he discovered that his evil value had skyrocketed. The figure, blood-red, had reached the terrifying number of [-99999].

Then, the system, which hadn't manifested in years, notified him that if the evil value reached [-100000], the host would be annihilated.

What was most detestable was that if the system detected a criminal case nearby and he didn't solve it, his evil value would also increase depending on the case's difficulty.

Clearly, they were scamming him!

Desperate, just when he was asking how to eliminate this evil value system, he had already arrived in this world of Conan.

At the dinner table, Heiji was somewhat distracted.

The method to reduce the evil value was simple: solve a case. Depending on the difficulty of the case, a corresponding amount of evil value would be eliminated.

This system was forcing him to be a detective.

"System, can the evil value only be reduced by solving cases?"

Although the world of Conan was full of cases, there had to be another way.

"There are other methods, but the host must discover them on their own." The system's voice was mechanical, devoid of any emotion.

"I have to discover them myself... I should never have gotten involved in this." Heiji sighed with regret.

"If it weren't for the system helping the host clean the scene, the host would have already been executed for murder."

Heiji had nothing to retort. But he didn't regret it. Just because he intervened in an injustice, that rich kid sent his thugs to cripple him. If he hadn't practiced martial arts, he'd already be invalid.

So, determined to go to the end, he thought about teaching that rich kid a lesson but ended up killing him by mistake.

The scene was full of his fingerprints, and escaping was impossible. Just when he thought he was going to pay with his life, the system appeared and saved him.

He was already bound, and it was impossible to get rid of it. If he didn't want to be annihilated, he could only try to reduce his evil value. However, finding a way to reduce it quickly—that was the real problem.
